A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original regression simulations and evaluations on News Popularity, Communities and Crime, Boston Housing, UPDRS, and Abalone.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulations and real-data evaluations, updates empirical estimates, and adds electricity-consumption results and Abalone fold-count experiments.

M1.justification: The aggregation procedures in equations (10), (12), and (14), threshold adjustment, and unequal-fold treatment are retained. Equation (9) repairs the existing smoothed-p-value formula; it does not establish a new algorithmic component or changed implementation.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds electricity-consumption regression with 35,411 observations and 20 covariates. The synthetic scenario and five original real-data applications remain. The Abalone fold-count expansion changes settings within existing coverage.

E2.justification: The new electricity comparison evaluates Bonferroni p-value merging at levels α and 2α, neither evaluated in v1. Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: Abalone evaluation expands from K = 10 to K = 5, 10, and 20. The electricity experiment introduces a 30,000/5,411 training/test allocation, 100-tree random forest, and K = 10, plus an uneven-split control allocating nine-tenths of the available data to model fitting.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds sensitivity analysis of Abalone set size and variability across fold counts. The electricity experiment also compares ordinary and uneven split conformal prediction, controlling the fitting-data fraction to examine the benefit of cross-conformal aggregation.

E5.justification: All five retained real-data applications explicitly increase repetitions from 20 to 100. Table 1 additionally reports coverage minima, maxima, and ranges across repetitions, whereas v1 reports only mean coverage. This substantially expands replication and coverage-variability reporting.

E6.justification: Real-data estimates are updated, generally retaining the earlier conclusions, and new fold-count and electricity results are added. Matching K = 10 Abalone experiments, eu-cross mean size/coverage changes from 5.512/0.836 in v1 Table 6 to 5.444/0.843 in v2 Table 7. These summaries use 20 versus 100 repetitions, so they do not establish an algorithmic performance gain.

T1.justification: Equation (9) restores a missing summation over strict-comparison indicators. Section 2 corrects the direction of the score/model symmetry implication, and Section 4 explicitly states exchangeable-data conditions for coverage guarantees. The main bounds and appendix proof arguments remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the central contribution: exchangeability and randomization produce smaller cross-conformal prediction sets while preserving the stated coverage guarantees. Added experiments and practical guidance do not redefine this claim.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds guidance on using α/2 for a 1−α guarantee, α when weaker coverage is acceptable, or ordinary modified cross-conformal prediction for intermediate needs. Remark 4.5 and Appendix E add explanations of mean versus Bonferroni merging under dependence, while Section 5.2 explicitly discusses coverage–size and coverage-variability tradeoffs.

D1.justification: Section 5 newly supplies a link to experiment code. Appendix E documents the electricity experiment's sample allocation, forest size, fold count, and uneven-split construction. The PDFs establish the added access information, not the repository's contents or accessibility.

R1.justification: v2 credits Saunders et al. (1999) for early conformal prediction and adds literature on covariate shift, relaxed assumptions, and prediction-set selection or aggregation. The central positioning around cross-conformal prediction and exchangeable p-value merging remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 makes local wording and terminology edits and expands related work, explanations, and practical discussion. The main section sequence and Appendices A–F remain intact; there is no extensive narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: Table 1 becomes a grouped mean/minimum/maximum/range display. Two additional Abalone tables and an electricity table are added; v1's K = 10 Table 6 corresponds to v2 Table 7. Captions gain explicit α settings, while the overall figure and table design remains similar.

improvement.justification: Increasing real-data repetitions from 20 to 100, reporting coverage variability, adding targeted controls, and supplying a code link improve empirical assessment and reproducibility. Formula corrections and coverage-level guidance also help. These are incremental gains; the new electricity discussion overstates eu-mod-cross's size advantage, since Table 9 reports 32.27 versus 26.52 for split conformal at 2α.
